ai.title: Remove ESLint fixAll from editor code actions on save
ai.summary: Removed source.fixAll.eslint from editor.codeActionsOnSave in .vscode/settings.json. Prevents ESLint from automatically fixing code on save, relying on manual linting or separate fix commands. Affects repository-wide VS Code editor configuration.

eli5.text: When you save a file in the editor, the code used to fix itself automatically in some ways that the team decided could cause confusion, so those auto-fixes have been turned off. Now you'll only see imports being cleaned up automatically when you save, and any other code issues will need to be fixed manually. You won't see any automatic changes beyond organizing your imports as you work.

ai.title: ai-sdk adapter enables Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic model routing
ai.summary: modelToAiSDKModel now routes geminiModels, openaiModels, and claudeModels to their respective @ai-sdk provider languageModel() calls. Previously only FinetunedVertexModel was mapped, throwing Unknown model for other providers. Change lives in backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts. Uses Object.values() membership checks against common/constants model enums.

eli5.text: You can now ask the assistant to use Google's Gemini, OpenAI, or Anthropic's Claude models, depending on which one your account is set to use. Before this change, trying to pick any of those models (other than one specific Google variant) would just fail with a generic error, because the system didn't know how to connect to them. Now, when you choose a model, the system checks which family it belongs to and sends your request to the matching service. The assistant behaves the same either way, so you might not notice the switch unless you're the kind of person who looks at which model answered.

ai.title: Add @ai-sdk/openai to backend deps
ai.summary: Added @ai-sdk/openai ^1.3.21 to backend/package.json dependencies. Sorted existing workspace deps alphabetically. Internal dependency update only. No user-facing changes.

eli5.text: The system now has a new set of building blocks that connect it to an outside artificial-intelligence company, so the assistant can talk to and use that company's models when the developers decide what to plug in. This does not change what you see today, but it gives the developers a ready path to switch the assistant over to that new provider later without rebuilding key parts. If you were to open the system's dependency list, you'd notice one more entry alongside the existing AI tools, and the list is now neatly organized alphabetically.

ai.title: Switch doc query to ai-sdk structured output
ai.summary: Documentation query moved from `promptFlashWithFallbacks` to `promptAiSdkStructured` using `generateObject` with Zod schema. Replaced manual JSON parsing and confidence float with boolean `relevant` flag. `ProjectAnalysis` interface updated to match schema. Covers `backend/src/get-documentation-for-query.ts` and `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts`.

eli5.text: The documentation search feature now relies on a standardized, schema-driven prompt mechanism that returns structured results (projectId, topic, and a simple yes/no relevance flag) instead of free-form text with a numerical confidence score. This only affects internal tooling used to find project documentation, so you won't see any visible difference in the product, but the system now parses responses more reliably by validating the expected fields automatically rather than manually interpreting raw output. The change is already live in the internal backend used by developers and automated systems.

ai.title: Refactor terminal check to Vercel AI SDK
ai.summary: checkTerminalCommand now uses promptAiSdk instead of racing promptOpenAI and promptFlashWithFallbacks. The prompt structure shifted to system/user roles, expecting 'y'/'n' responses parsed via includes('y'). This simplifies the logic by removing the Promise.race timeout handling for multiple providers, relying solely on a single AI SDK call with a 30s timeout. Internal refactor affecting backend/src/check-terminal-command.ts.

eli5.text: The assistant now identifies whether something is a terminal command using a single, unified system instead of trying two different AI systems and picking whichever responded first. If you interact with the assistant, you won't notice any difference in behavior; it still correctly recognizes commands like "git pull" or "npm install" and rejects casual requests like "run cargo check." Behind the scenes, the code is simpler and easier to maintain, relying on one provider instead of racing two, but your experience stays exactly the same.

ai.title: Refine terminal command and documentation agent prompts
ai.summary: Prompt structure updated for terminal command and documentation agents. `check-terminal-command.ts` consolidates system and user messages into a single user role with explicit prompt delimiters. `get-documentation-for-query.ts` replaces boolean relevance flags with 0-1 confidence scores, updating `ProjectAnalysis` and `zodSchema` types. Logic now gates documentation retrieval on `confidence <= 0.7` instead of `!relevant`.

eli5.text: When someone types something that looks like a command you'd run in a terminal, the system will now be better at telling the difference between an actual command and a sentence describing one (like 'run cargo check'). In plain words: the behind-the-scenes prompts the system uses to make these decisions were fine-tuned for accuracy and clarity. No settings to change and nothing to download. This is already live today.

eli5.text: Gemini is now instructed to draft its code changes and planning documents within its thinking stream before taking action. This only affects the internal backend prompt configuration, and since the instructions are untested, they have no observable impact today. If you checked the backend prompt, you'd see two new lines telling Gemini to write out its code and planning steps before executing them.

ai.title: Enable Gemini 2.5 Pro in experimental mode

New `start-experimental` npm scripts added to root and `npm-app` package.json to launch CLI with `--experimental` flag.

eli5.text: The assistant can now use a newer model when you launch it in the experimental mode, and file-request tasks in that same mode use a more capable model too. Two new start commands let you run the assistant with the experimental flag turned on without typing it manually. This only takes effect when you explicitly choose the experimental mode; normal use is unchanged.

eli5.text: The assistant was told to stop referencing its own 'Buffy' persona in its responses and to avoid mentioning tool names or parameters to users. If you interacted with the assistant after this change, you'd notice it's less likely to act flamboyantly as 'Buffy' and won't explain which tools it's using behind the scenes. This only affects the assistant's internal instructions and doesn't change how any feature works.

ai.title: main-prompt: pass userInstructions only on full prompt
ai.summary: backend/src/main-prompt.ts now gates userInstructions injection on prompt presence. When prompt is absent, content falls back to costMode toolsInstructions plus toolInstructions instead. Internal prompt assembly refactor. Scope: backend main-prompt only.

eli5.text: When you give the system a full, detailed request, it now uses your exact instructions to shape how the assistant responds. When you don't supply that detailed request, the assistant instead falls back to a simpler, pre-set set of guidance built from cost-control rules and internal tools. This only affects how prompts are assembled behind the scenes in the backend; you wouldn't see a new setting or menu, but the assistant's behavior may feel slightly different depending on whether you provide a full prompt.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.270
ai.summary: Version incremented to 1.0.270. Change applied to npm-app/package.json. Routine release step.

eli5.text: Your assistant can now talk to new AI models directly, including Google Gemini and the latest Claude and OpenAI options. When you ask it to read documentation, check terminal commands, or reason through a plan, it routes through a unified system that picks the best model for the job instead of racing separate providers. The Gemini 2.5 Pro model is now reachable in experimental mode, and the assistant's planning prompts were refined so it drafts code and steps more reliably. These changes went live in version 1.0.270 on May 6, 2025.

ai.title: Gate toolsInstructions to experimental costMode
ai.summary: mainPrompt gates toolsInstructions injection behind costMode === 'experimental'. Default cost modes now omit tool instructions from userInstructions array. Adds explicit proceed directive to prompt. Affects backend/src/main-prompt.ts.

eli5.text: The system now hides advanced tool instructions from most conversations, showing them only in the experimental mode. If you're not using that special mode, you won't see the detailed technical guidance that helps the assistant use extra tools, making interactions simpler and more straightforward. This is already live for anyone using the default settings.

ai.title: Fix experimental mode prompt filtering and instruction assembly
ai.summary: Corrects `costMode` logic in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. The previous filter incorrectly excluded system instructions only in experimental mode; the condition is inverted to `costMode !== 'experimental'`. The user message construction now explicitly branches on `prompt` and `costMode` to ensure `toolsInstructions` are included only when appropriate, preventing malformed or missing instruction blocks.

eli5.text: When you're working in the experimental mode, the assistant was accidentally dropping important system instructions that tell it how to behave. Now it keeps those instructions and also builds the message it receives a bit more carefully, so the tools and directions are stitched together correctly instead of being left out or mangled. If you use the experimental mode today, the assistant should follow its special setup instructions properly instead of silently ignoring them.

ai.title: tools.ts forbids XML entities in tool call format
ai.summary: Added rule 4 to backend/src/tools.ts instructing agents to avoid XML entities (<, >, &) in tool call parameters, requiring raw characters instead. This prevents parsing errors caused by uninterpreted entities. Scope limited to backend tool definition instructions. Rule 4 is now included in the critical failure warning.

eli5.text: When you ask an AI assistant to act on your behalf using special XML-formatted commands, you may have noticed occasional errors if those commands accidentally contained characters like <, >, or &. Developers have now added a clear warning (the fourth rule) telling the assistant to always use plain <, >, and & symbols instead of special XML-encoded versions (<, >, &) in its tool calls. This rule is now explicitly listed in the failure warning shown to the assistant before it attempts a tool call, making it harder to accidentally trigger a parsing failure. This change is already live in today's build.

ai.title: Fix gitignore subdirectory pattern resolution in project-file-tree
ai.summary: Non-rooted gitignore patterns now prepend `relativeDirPath` before matching, ensuring correct resolution for nested `.gitignore` files. Previously, patterns lacking a leading slash were treated as project-root-relative, causing incorrect ignore behavior in subdirectories. This change applies to `common/src/project-file-tree.ts` within the Shared/Core package.

eli5.text: When you place a.gitignore file inside a subfolder of a larger project, the tool that builds the file list was ignoring the wrong files because it treated every ignore rule as if it lived at the project's top level. Now the rule is first adjusted to the folder it actually belongs to, stripping any leading slash and tacking on the subfolder path, so files in the right place get skipped while others remain visible. If you have nested.gitignore files, you'll notice fewer surprises about which files show up or get excluded from your project view.

ai.title: Disable Gemini 2.5 Pro thinking in normal/max cost modes
ai.summary: Gemini 2.5 Pro streaming disables thinking by passing `thinkingBudget: 0` when `costMode` is 'normal' or 'max'. `streamGemini25ProWithFallbacks` accepts `thinkingBudget` in options and forwards it to `promptGeminiStream`. Scope limited to `backend/src/llm-apis/gemini-with-fallbacks.ts` and `backend/src/prompt-agent-stream.ts`. `thinkingBudget` remains `undefined` for other cost modes, preserving default thinking behavior.

eli5.text: You won't see a difference unless you use advanced settings: Gemini 2.5 Pro now skips its "thinking" step by default when running in normal or max performance modes, which keeps responses faster and simpler. Behind the scenes, it turns off step-by-step planning for those modes while leaving it enabled for other modes.
